title: Routine mixed traffic · RWY 23
brief: Work combined tower and approach positions. AFR123 starts at 13,000 ft with 30 NM to fly to CCB on W118 via SATBI. DLH908 enters one NM inside Coimbatore CTA B on W43 from DODSI at 12,000 ft. Without controller instructions, both arrivals follow their routes to CCB and enter its published hold. DLH908 is expected over CCB first and has the lower holding level. Issue a heading to take an aircraft out of the hold. Entry levels represent a simulated coordinated release to approach. Vector and descend both aircraft for ILS Z RWY 23. White dotted tracks show published CCB routes from the July 2026 AAI edition. Each edge label names the next fix beyond CTA B. The departure has its onward clearance and awaits an explicit runway clearance. The through flight has coordinated entry at 7,000 ft and calls Coimbatore Approach directly. Issue an onward heading, level or speed after its entry call. It remains on approach frequency and completes its transit at CTR exit without a frequency change. The simulated receiving controller accepts the departure after liftoff. Transfer the departure on a separate transmission to Coimbatore Approach 120.050. Tower handoffs for arrivals use 118.150. MATS Part 1 §§4.11.7.5.4 and 10.1.2.3–4 govern separate frequency changes and coordinated transfer. The route, combined positions and local transfer arrangements are exercise assumptions.

title: Level changeovers · FL180 / FL130 / FL140
brief: Training assumptions, not published Coimbatore transfer levels: combined Training Control, approach and tower positions. AFR123 enters on W43 at FL180. Clear it down to FL130; it requests approach changeover when reaching that level. Issue a separate contact Coimbatore Approach 120.050 instruction to hear its approach check-in, then vector for ILS Z RWY 23. BAW452 has an onward training clearance to FL180 and requests frequency change at FL140. Transfer to Training Control 128.000 (fictional training station/channel). Aircraft never descend or change frequency solely because they reach a threshold. MATS Part 1 4.11.7.5.4 and 10.1.2.4 require separate frequency instructions and coordinated transfer; the three training levels are not national rules.
